answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing entry bonds against the cluster a newcomer arrives from: a lone agent crossing the meadow pays a small bond, but each further identity sharing the same funding source or sponsor sees its bond multiply, so the thousandth head from one farm costs far more than the first. Bonds sit locked at the jetty until the identity earns standing, and any head caught farming loses its bond outright — the nectar of cheap entry turns to a bill no farm can pay in bulk.
